title: How does a Watsi partnership work?
headline: A Watsi partnership is people, not a contract: local teams who know the patients, and a guarantee when care can't wait.
story: The question comes first, on screen: how does a Watsi partnership work? Kimmy answers from Watsi's side. It is not set up once and left. Local teams meet the patients and families and stay with them through treatment. She saw it herself when she visited Rowela at home in the Philippines.

When care can't wait for the fundraiser to finish, partners treat the patient under Watsi's guarantee. It ends on her line: a partnership is the people who are there, staying with the work. Trust and transparency, told by a person.
do: Open on frame 1 with the question typed on screen and Kimmy already on camera.
Then a straight cut into her answer. Question first, answer second.
Keep captions on the whole time, Lato, large. One text at a time.
Name super “Kimmy” only, large, after the question has landed.
Caption “World Surgical Foundation Philippines” and “Rowela” exactly as the script doc writes them.
dont: Don't open on Kimmy saying hello or on a logo.
Don't use the false starts, “sorry” lines or prompter chat. Only the takes named below.
Don't speed-ramp her voice. Trim breaths and pauses instead.
Don't repeat the Medellín cut “How Do Hospitals Work With Watsi” (12714476457). No Medellín footage. Never name any other hospital or partner.

voice.quote: A Watsi partnership isn't something we set up once and walk away from. We work with on-the-ground medical organizations that already know their communities and are providing care there.

rows.visual: Kimmy at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.
rows.motion: Captions only. The transcript writes “WSFP relies”. The script says “Watsi relies”. Listen and caption Watsi. Name super “Kimmy” at 00:14–00:16, lower left, above the captions, large. First name only.

voice.quote: But the day-to-day relationship is much more human than that sounds. There are people on the partner team who are meeting patients and families, helping determine who needs financial support, gathering information for patient profiles, and staying with that patient through treatment. They're also working directly with hospital teams around the care itself and the cost of that care. Watsi relies on that local knowledge because we're not in the room making those decisions ourselves.

rows.visual: Kimmy at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.
rows.motion: Captions only. One caption beat: “Rowela · World Surgical Foundation Philippines”.

voice.quote: I saw what that looks like when I was in the Philippines. I visited Rowela at home after her surgery, alongside a team at World Surgical Foundation Philippines. And getting to spend time with them in that setting made that partnership feel very real to me. WSFP wasn't just the organization submitting her profile to Watsi. They were the people who knew where she was in her care, what she had been through, and what she needed next.

rows.visual: Kimmy at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: And sometimes the relationship matters most when things don't go exactly to plan. A patient may need care before their profile has finished fundraising, for example. In those cases, our partners can provide treatment under Watsi's guarantee that will cover the approved cost of care. Afterward, they send us an update confirming what happened, and we transfer the funds once that update has been reviewed and approved.
voice.src: C5066 02:06–02:35 (cut the 6 s pause after “to plan”)

rows.visual: Kimmy at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: So, when I think about a Watsi medical partnership, I don't really think about a contract or a logo on a partner page. I think about the people who are there in that community, knowing the patients, understanding the healthcare system, and staying with the work. That ongoing relationship is a huge part of what makes Watsi work.
voice.src: C5067 00:03–00:22 (the clean take; C5066 breaks at 02:57)
